title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 15
paragraphs: Of those who remained in their places in the sea-fight, the Chians suffered very severely, since they displayed brilliant feats of valor and refused to play the coward. These, as has been said, furnished one hundred ships, and in each of them forty picked men of their citizens served as marines. When they saw the greater number of their allies deserting them, they did not think it fit to behave like the cowards among them, but, left with only a few allies, they continued to fight and kept breaking through the enemy's line; until at last, after having defeated many of the enemy's ships, they lost the greater number of their own.
